claims.text: Arc melting followed by drop-casting can be used to prepare FeNiCrMn HEA samples for tensile testing.
Drop-casting ensures a homogeneous FeNiCrMn microstructure.
The proposed processing route will permit reliable measurement of yield strength and ductility.
The FeNiCrMn alloy's mechanical performance may be enhanced by solid-solution strengthening.
Conventionally melted FeNiCrMn HEAs have coarse dendritic structures.
FeNiCrMn HEAs have known excellent corrosion resistance.
The mechanical properties of FeNiCrMn HEAs are uncharacterized or poorly characterized.
Arc melting and drop-casting will produce FeNiCrMn ingots with refined, homogeneous microstructures.
Arc-melted and drop-cast HEAs can be subjected to room-temperature tensile testing at a controlled strain rate.
The proposed FeNiCrMn specimens can be tensile-tested at elevated temperatures up to approximately 700 °C.
SEM and TEM characterization before and after testing can establish the relevant FeNiCrMn microstructural changes.
Controlled solidification during drop-casting establishes grain size and phase uniformity.
Grain size and phase uniformity mediate dislocation motion and solid-solution strengthening.
Arc melting produces a homogeneous BCC/FCC solid solution in FeNiCrMn.
A homogeneous FeNiCrMn solid solution promotes solid-solution strengthening and possibly grain-boundary strengthening.
These strengthening mechanisms will produce measurable yield strength and ductility during tensile deformation.
Tensile testing will yield distinct values of yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, and ductility.
The tensile properties of drop-cast FeNiCrMn will differ from those of baseline coarse as-cast material.
Existing FeNiCrMn literature mainly reports corrosion resistance and provides little or no quantitative mechanical data.
Casting defects, insufficient microstructural refinement, and cooling-rate variation may prevent the proposed route from revealing intrinsic mechanical properties.
